checked.claim: Amendment passed 10 July 2026, promulgated 17 July 2026, in force within two years, not in force on 2 October 2026
checked.evidence: PPC page: 令和８年７月10日の国会において可決、成立し; 令和８年７月17日に公布. One Asia Lawyers and Baker McKenzie: effective within two years of promulgation. No entry-into-force date published.

checked.claim: Current criminal penalties; surcharge under new Arts 148-3 to 148-17 equal to financial benefit, not applying where 1,000 or fewer affected, reasonable care, insignificant harm
checked.evidence: One Asia: Arts 148-3 to 148-17, surcharge equivalent to the financial benefit from the violation, within two years. Baker McKenzie: amount equals consideration received; exemptions where fewer than 1,000 people affected, reasonable care, or insignificant harm as set by enforcement regulations; applies only to designated serious violations. Exact threshold wording not checked against the statute.
checked.replacement: Today the PPC cannot impose monetary penalties. Money penalties come only through criminal prosecution: breach of a PPC order carries up to one year's imprisonment or a fine up to JPY 1 million for individuals (Article 178) and a fine up to JPY 100 million for the company (Article 184); false reporting carries a fine up to JPY 500,000 (map: court). The 2026 amendment adds an administrative surcharge imposed by the PPC itself (new Articles 148-3 to 148-17), equal to the financial benefit from certain designated serious violations, with exemptions for small-scale cases (reported as fewer than 1,000 individuals affected), reasonable care or insignificant harm; it will start within two years of 17 July 2026.

checked.claim: Surcharge calculated as the profit gained, excludes cases affecting 1,000 or fewer
checked.evidence: PPC outline: penalties 'equivalent to the pecuniary benefits obtained'; Baker McKenzie: 'consideration received', exemption below 1,000 individuals. 'Profit' overstates the precision; threshold wording unconfirmed.
checked.replacement: The planned surcharge equals the financial benefit obtained from the violation, not a percentage of turnover, and small-scale cases (reported as fewer than 1,000 people affected) are excluded.
